entries.appliesTo: any person offering therapy or psychotherapy services to the public (including via Internet-based AI) and Maine-licensed mental health professionals using AI for administrative or supplementary support

dutySources.disclosure-ui: Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(3)(A) — 'The client or the client's legally authorized representative is informed in writing of the following: (1) That artificial intelligence will be used'
dutySources.consent-workflow: Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(3)(B) — 'The client or the client's legally authorized representative provides consent to the use of artificial intelligence.'
dutySources.human-review: Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(4) — 'A licensee may not allow artificial intelligence to: … C. Generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without review and approval by the licensee.'

sources.aiTherapyRule: Sec. 1, 10 MRSA §1500-EE(2) — 'A person may not provide, advertise or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet-based artificial intelligence, to the public unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are provided by a licensed professional.'
sources.consentRequired: Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(3)(B) — 'The client or the client's legally authorized representative provides consent to the use of artificial intelligence.'
sources.scope: Sec. 1, 10 MRSA §1500-EE(1)(D) — '"Therapy or psychotherapy services" means services provided to diagnose, treat or address an individual's mental health or behavioral health through therapeutic communication.'
sources.enforcer: Sec. 1, 10 MRSA §1500-EE(3) — 'A violation of subsection 2 is a violation of the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act.' ; Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(8) — 'A violation of this section is subject to disciplinary action by the board pursuant to Title 10, section 8003, subsection 5.'

flags: aiTherapyRule=ban is slightly lossy: AI may not provide therapeutic communication or make independent therapeutic decisions (§2113(4)), but licensees may use AI for administrative support and, with consent, supplementary support (§2113(2)-(3)) — a supervised carve-out for non-therapeutic tasks
Secs. 2-8 enact a verbatim-identical AI-support regime across seven Title 32 licensing chapters (§§2113, 2600-G, 3300-J, 3820-A, 6207-D, 7009, 13870); coded once
supplementary-support use additionally conditioned on session recording/transcription: §2113(3) — 'only when the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed'

no listed duty fits: denial-of-treatment prohibition (§2113(5) — 'may not deny, or refuse to provide, therapy or psychotherapy services … on the sole basis that the client has not provided consent'), confidentiality-compliance mandate (§2113(6)), client-waiver voidness (§2113(11)), and preserved private right of action for harm/negligence (§2113(12))
boards must adopt major substantive implementing rules (§2113(10)) — future rulemaking not coded
